# THE RECORD of how every row of production's migration ledger,
# supabase_migrations.schema_migrations, lines up with supabase/migrations/.
# Issue #91. Read reconcile-ledger.js for the mechanism, the export query and
# the verdict vocabulary; run `node scripts/schema-check/reconcile-ledger.js
# check` (also run by reconcile-ledger.test.ts under `npm test`) to hold this
# file against the repo.
# Columns, tab-separated: version  name  verdict  file  note
#   version  the ledger's version string: 14 digits for a run through the MCP
#            server or the CLI, 0XX for a CLI push of a numbered file, `?` for
#            a row known by name only (named on #78 or in a file header) whose
#            version the export has not supplied yet, `-` for a repo file row.
#   name     the ledger's name column; `?` when only the version is known.
#   verdict  tracked | recovered-by | consolidated-by | number-collision |
#            missing-file | no-ledger-row (defined in reconcile-ledger.js).
#   file     the supabase/migrations file the verdict names, if any.
#   note     evidence, by file:line where it lives in the repo.
# STATUS 2026-10-20. The export exists: @slowdog-dev ran it on 2026-10-17 and
# imported it in PR #97, version and name only, no statements column. Every
# row below has since been read against the repo, and the label the import
# step writes before a person has read a row is gone (the test holds that).
# What the read established:
#   * Most 14-digit rows are a file's own run through the Supabase MCP server
#     under the file's name, and the file is their record (tracked).
#   * The 2026-08-05 session's rows are consolidated by 008 and 009, assigned
#     by content: 008 holds the two functions, the column and the constraint,
#     009 the three policies and every RPC gate.
#   * Three collisions are renumberings, not missing files: 014_relay_failures
#     is 015, 018_discord_bridge_opt_out is 017 and
#     019_save_count_trigger_and_backfill is 020. 031_insert_grants_and_
#     corrections is 031's second run, folded into the committed file.
#   * Six rows have no file and need their `statements` column before a
#     migration can be written for any of them. The query that supplies them:
#       select version, name, statements
#       from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations
#       where name in (
#         'pin_search_path_on_security_definer_functions',
#         'fix_publish_draft_sequence_search_path',
#         'optimize_rls_policies_sequences_comments',
#         'optimize_rls_policies_remaining_tables',
#         'add_indexes_for_hot_query_paths',
#         'backfill_display_name_from_username')
#       order by version;
#   * The ledger ends at 037 (2026-09-17). Everything from 038 on, and a few
#     earlier files, was applied by hand and has no row (no-ledger-row).
#   * Outside the ledger: four triggers production had that no file created
#     until 049 (found by PR #98's trigger test), and the `avatars` storage
#     bucket, created in the dashboard with neither a row nor a file
# A text comparison of the tracked rows against their files is still owed,
# since the export carried no statements; the 018 and 022 rows say so.
# Nothing in this file is a migration. Writing a migration for a missing-file
# row needs that row's `statements` column, which only the export carries.
